observations.body: The psalm praises steadfast love, recalls covenant with David, expands God’s rule, quotes the promise, then laments rejection, broken walls, shortened youth, and asks how long.
observations.label: Covenant praise turns into protest over the crown: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps the psalmist, the LORD, David, the anointed king, enemies, and the people, heavens, sea, throne, broken defenses, and royal shame in poetic space, praising, recalling covenant, quoting promise, rejecting, breaching defenses, lamenting, asking, and blessing visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read Psalms 89:1–52 as its own royal, poetic, and prophetic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places the Davidic covenant is recited inside a prayer that says the crown has been cast down inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
